skill.name: workflow-orchestration-patterns

skill.summary: Design Temporal workflows with clear activity boundaries, saga compensation, deterministic state handling, and resilience practices.

content.value_statement: Distributed workflows are difficult to make durable, deterministic, and recoverable. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Temporal patterns for reliable orchestration.
actual_capabilities: Explains when Temporal is a good fit for long-running workflows.
Separates workflow orchestration logic from activity side effects.
Outlines saga compensation, entity workflows, fan-out, and async callbacks.
Summarizes determinism rules for time, randomness, I/O, and external calls.
Lists retry, idempotency, heartbeat, monitoring, and scaling practices.
limitations: Focuses on Temporal concepts, not other orchestration engines.
Does not include a runnable reference application.
Provides architectural guidance, not production configuration for a specific cluster.
Requires users to validate patterns against their language SDK.

use_cases.title: Design order fulfillment workflows
use_cases.description: Use saga steps and compensation rules for inventory, payment, and fulfillment services.

use_cases.title: Plan resilient infrastructure automation
use_cases.description: Define workflow boundaries, child workflows, retries, and monitoring for deployment pipelines.

use_cases.title: Review Temporal architecture decisions
use_cases.description: Check workflow determinism, activity idempotency, and long-running process boundaries before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a workflow pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: I am new to Temporal. Help me decide whether my process should use a workflow. Ask for missing goals, steps, and failure rules.

prompt_templates.title: Separate workflows and activities
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this process: [describe process]. Identify workflow decisions, activity calls, retries, and idempotency requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Design a saga workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Temporal saga for [business process]. Include forward steps, compensation steps, failure handling, and verification checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an existing architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Temporal design: [paste architecture]. Find determinism risks, versioning concerns, scaling limits, and missing operational metrics.

output_examples.input: A team wants to orchestrate inventory reservation, payment capture, and fulfillment.
output: Register inventory release before reservation, refund before payment capture, and cancellation before fulfillment.
Use idempotency keys for every activity.

output_examples.input: A workflow uses current system time and direct API calls inside orchestration logic.
output: Move direct API calls into activities.
Replace system time with deterministic workflow time.
Add tests that replay workflow history after code changes.

output_examples.input: A product team needs human approval before account changes expire.
output: Use the async callback pattern with signals.
Set an approval timeout and define the expiration path.
Record approval state through workflow queries.

best_practices: Keep workflow code deterministic and move side effects into activities.
Register compensation before each saga step executes.
Set activity timeouts, retries, heartbeats, and idempotency keys deliberately.
anti_patterns: Calling external APIs directly from workflow code.
Using system time, random values, or global state in workflow logic.
Leaving activities without timeouts or retry classification.

faq.question: What does this skill help me design?
faq.answer: It helps design Temporal workflows, activities, saga compensation, retries, and deterministic orchestration boundaries.

faq.question: Is this skill only for Temporal?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written around Temporal concepts and API patterns.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance, review prompts, and implementation checklists.

faq.question: How does it support failure recovery?
faq.answer: It explains retry policies, idempotent activities, compensation steps, and heartbeat patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with microservice transactions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers saga orchestration for multi-service workflows and distributed transactions.

faq.question: What should I provide in my prompt?
faq.answer: Provide process steps, external systems, failure rules, timeouts, and consistency requirements.
